title: Select the authorization boundary for the first read-only release
decision_needed: Choose whether caller identity must be enforced at the application gateway or at both the gateway and retrieval projection.
execution_unlocked: The implementation owner can finalize the authentication design and test plan.

recipient.authority_reason: Owns the authentication boundary and exception policy.

why_now.delay_consequence: Implementation and threat-model review remain blocked.

material_unknowns: Whether defense-in-depth identity enforcement is mandatory for this data class.
assumptions: The gateway and retrieval projection can both receive caller identity.

options.label: Gateway enforcement only
options.action: Enforce caller identity at the application gateway.
options.why_viable: The gateway is already the authenticated request boundary.
risks: A projection-path defect could bypass intended filtering
assumptions: All retrieval traffic passes through the gateway
exceptions: Not suitable for direct projection access
options.reversibility: Can add projection enforcement later with interface changes.

options.label: Gateway and projection enforcement
options.action: Enforce caller identity at both boundaries.
options.why_viable: Both components can receive caller identity.
assumptions: A shared policy contract can be maintained
exceptions: May be unnecessary for public-only sources
options.reversibility: One enforcement point can be removed after review.
options.execution_after_selection: Implementation owner defines the shared policy contract.

recommendation.rationale: The protected data boundary benefits from defense in depth.
disconfirming_evidence: The first release is read-only and all traffic is expected through the gateway.

primary_question: Should the first release use option A or option B?
minimum_response: Reply A or B; reply defer until <fact> only if the missing policy fact changes the choice.
fallback_behavior: Do not implement either boundary by silence; escalate the missing policy decision at the stage gate.
follow_ups: If B, must both boundaries use one shared policy artifact?

inference: Defense in depth likely lowers bypass risk.
uncertainty: Mandatory policy for this data class is not yet confirmed.
